title: AWS CLI credentials and config
whyItMatters: AWS access keys and session settings in this folder can be used to act as the account owner against cloud resources.
notes: Covers credentials, config and cached SSO tokens in subfolders. Nothing inside is read; macOS Keychain is not consulted.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy the credentials and config files named in the plan to a safe place if you still need those keys.
cleanup.signOut: In the AWS console deactivate and then delete the access keys this Mac used, under IAM > Users > Security credentials.
steps: Sign in to the AWS console and find the access key that belongs to this Mac.
Deactivate the key, test that nothing still needs it, then delete it.
Delete the folder named in the plan, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Scripts and tools that used these keys stop working; keys left active still grant access from any copy.
cleanup.source: AWS CLI User Guide, Configuration and credential file settings: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html
